oneLine: Answers 'can this site handle the demand in this window?': it keeps the volume forecast, works out path capacity and labour needed, plans and announces any shortage.

rows.title: Declare how fast one station works
rows.story: An operator states how much one station of a process handles per hour at a site. The station counts from the floor map are multiplied by this figure when a path's capacity is worked out.

rows.title: Declare the labour a dock booking costs
rows.story: An operator states how many labour minutes a dock appointment, and each shipment notice on it, costs at a site for a process path. Without it, bookings add no labour demand and the plan says so.

rows.title: Keep the process flows behind the plans
rows.story: The hand-made process path list is retired and said goodbye at its old address. The steps a plan follows now arrive only as flows kept current whenever process-path-management changes a path.
rows.policy: Whenever a process path changes, refresh this warehouse's copy of its steps.

rows.title: Register a capacity limit by hand
rows.story: A planner records one limit on a process at a location for a time window: labour, location, equipment, station, conveyor, buffer or replenishment. The lowest limit is what the process can really do. An announcement goes out only if that figure moves.

rows.title: Receive the volume forecast for a path
rows.story: A planner sends how many units a process path at a site is due to receive by each cut-off. A new forecast replaces the old one whole; sending the same one again changes nothing. No other context reads the announcement yet.

rows.title: Draft a capacity plan
rows.story: A planner asks whether a path can handle the demand at a site in a window. Demand is typed in, read from expected orders or from the volume forecast. Several drafts of one window are what-if options to compare side by side.

then.does: keeps the plan's window as a draft in its planned-capacity copy

rows.title: Publish a plan and announce any shortage
rows.story: Publishing makes a draft plan official, once only, and replaces the plan published before it for the same site, path and window. If the path can do less than the demand, the shortage and the slowest step are announced too.

then.does: marks the window published, retires a replaced plan and flags orders in a shortage; moves no promise
keeps the newest published plan window per site; plans without a site are skipped

rows.title: Commit the labour plan for a shift
rows.story: A planner commits rate, heads and hours for a path in a shift. Heads cannot exceed the stations installed; left out, they are worked out from the forecast. If workforce-management committed different heads, the gap is flagged, never corrected.

then.does: keeps a copy of the required heads per path and shift and proposes heads from it

rows.title: Turn committed shifts into labour limits
rows.story: Each line of a committed shift plan says how many people work a path, at what rate, for how many hours. That becomes a labour limit from the shift start for those hours. The rate is assumed to be units per hour.
rows.policy: Whenever a shift plan line is committed, register its heads times rate as a labour limit for its hours

rows.title: Compare committed heads with the labour plan
rows.story: A committed shift line that names its shift also records the heads workforce-management put on the path. If they differ from the labour plan, and the gap is new, it is flagged. Neither side is changed and nothing outside reads the flag yet.
rows.policy: Whenever a shift line is committed, store its heads and flag a new gap from the labour plan

rows.title: Keep the labour standards
rows.story: labor-performance announces how many seconds a pick, pack or label task should take, per site or for all sites. This service keeps every version and uses the one in force for a plan's window to state the labour each step needs.
rows.policy: Whenever a labour standard is defined or revised, add it to the local copy

rows.title: Keep the process flows
rows.story: process-path-management announces each flow: the stages a path passes through, in order. A newer version replaces an older one, so repeats and late arrivals are harmless. Path capacity reads these flows first.
rows.policy: Whenever a flow is defined, revised or retired, keep the newer version in the local copy

rows.title: Count a new slot on the floor
rows.story: facility-layout announces each slot. Storage slots add storage positions and work-center slots add stations, per zone. Station counts are multiplied by the declared station standard when a path's capacity is worked out.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is registered, add it to its zone's count of storage positions or stations

rows.title: Remove a retired slot from the count
rows.story: When facility-layout takes a slot out of service, it comes out of its zone's count. The count only ever follows the floor map and registers no capacity limit itself.
rows.policy: Whenever a slot is decommissioned, take it off its zone's count of positions or stations

rows.title: Keep the expected-orders list
rows.story: Each allocated order, fully or partly, counts once at its latest promise cutoff toward the demand of the site its event names, or of the configured site when it names none. Cancellations are not seen, so the figure can overstate demand.
rows.policy: Whenever an order is allocated, fully or partly, record it at its promise cutoff for its own or the configured site

rows.title: Keep the dock-bookings list
rows.story: dock-scheduling announces bookings, moves, cancellations and no-shows. Each has a version and the newest wins, so a cancellation that arrives first still sticks. Cancelled and missed bookings stop counting as demand.
rows.policy: Whenever a dock appointment is booked, moved, cancelled or missed, update the dock-booking demand copy

rows.title: Count what the floor really completes
rows.story: Completed tasks are counted per process step and minute. A plan's variance view sets them against the planned capacity. It is advice only and never changes a plan.
rows.policy: Whenever a task is completed, add it to the count for its process step and minute

rows.title: Feed the plan reports
rows.story: The service reads its own plan announcements and keeps daily facts for the reports: bottleneck frequency, shortage trend and plan throughput. A replaced plan still counts as published there.
rows.policy: Whenever a plan is created or published, add it to the plan facts behind the reports

hotspots.text: A shift event carries no window start and no rate unit field. The window is the event time plus planned hours, and the rate is taken as units per hour.
Task completions carry no site, so every completion goes to one configured site.
Orders whose event names no site still go to one configured site, and cancellations are not netted, so demand can be overstated.
Stations counted without a declared station standard only raise a warning. No throughput is invented for them.
Paths declared here by hand and flows from process-path-management live side by side until a live check shows every local path has a flow.
ProcessCapacityRegistered and ProcessCapacityChanged are published, but their consumer is marked as not built yet.

opportunities.text: Adjusting planned capacity automatically from observed throughput is left to a later decision, which must show it cannot oscillate.
